summary: This is a Mol Labs public research discussion card (N17) proposing a PC12 neurite-outgrowth assay to test whether Hericium erinaceus extract retains residual neurite phenotype under NGF neutralization or TrkA blockade that abolishes an NGF-class positive control. The document is a hypothesis/proposal (execution_status=NOT_RUN), cataloguing existing literature as baselines and identifying a key experimental gap: no published head-to-head study has co-designed an NGF-class abolish gate with a residual Hericium arm on the same panel. The project is at TRL 1–2 (concept with literature framing, no experimental data generated).

content_blocks.title: Document Overview and Status
content_blocks.content: Mol Labs public report card N17. Status: NEGATIVE (status_labels), execution_status=NOT_RUN. The document is a research discussion / hypothesis proposal (openlabs_target=discussion, openlabs_topic=neuroscience-brain, risk_class=research-discussion). It is tagged as nootropics, brain-longevity. No experiments have been run; this is a pre-registered assay proposal.

content_blocks.title: Central Claim / Hypothesis
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered PC12 neurite-outgrowth panel with an NGF-class positive control, NGF neutralization or TrkA blockade that abolishes NGF-class neurite gain, and a Hericium erinaceus extract (or named hericenone/erinacine prep) arm: under the same block that abolishes NGF-class neurite gain, Hericium retains residual neurite phenotype ≥50% of Hericium-alone (neurite-bearing % or neurite length units as pre-specified; α/N pre-specified). This is framed as an 'assumption-kill / ngf-insufficiency' test.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Hericium erinaceus is commonly framed via NGF induction (in 1321N1 astrocytes and mouse hippocampus) or NGF-mediated neurite potentiation in PC12 cells. Human cognition arms in published RCTs lack NGF/TrkA pharmacodynamics. No published study co-designs an abolish-NGF-class / residual-Hericium panel. The proposed experiment asks whether residual Hericium neurite phenotype on PC12 survives NGF neutralization or TrkA blockade that abolishes an NGF-class positive-control gain — i.e., whether NGF/TrkA is necessary for Hericium's neurite phenotype.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Baseline
content_blocks.content:
Four key prior art references are catalogued:
1. PMID 18844328 (Mori 2009, DOI 10.1002/ptr.2634): Yamabushitake MCI RCT; HDS-R improved vs placebo over 16 weeks, fell after washout. Human cognition without NGF PD / no TrkA-block arm; not residual-under-block H2H.
2. PMID 18758067 (Mori/Kawagishi 2008, DOI 10.1248/bpb.31.1727): H. erinaceus extract ↑ NGF mRNA/protein in 1321N1 astrocytes; hippocampal NGF mRNA ↑ in mice; conditioned medium enhanced PC12 neurites; hericenones C/D/E failed NGF gene induction. Cell/animal NGF induction prior; not residual-under-block H2H.
3. PMID 32581767 (Li 2020, DOI 10.3389/fnagi.2020.00155): Erinacine A–enriched Hericium mycelia mild-AD RCT 49 weeks; MMSE/IADL/neuroimaging; biomarkers include BDNF, Aβ1-40, apoE4, ACT — NGF not listed; no TrkA/NGF-block residual arm. BDNF pathway ≠ NGF mediation.
4. PMID 26481911 (Zhang 2015, DOI 10.1016/j.bmcl.2015.10.016): Hericium constituents stimulate/potentiate NGF-mediated neurite outgrowth on PC12 (in presence of NGF). Potentiation context prior; not residual under block that abolishes NGF-class gain.
Additional adjacent references noted but not matching: PMID 28758954, PMID 25288148, PMID 33066380 (TrkA/Erk potentiation, partial K252a on hericenone+low-NGF, TrkA-dependent erinacine C) — none co-design NGF-class positive control abolished by the same block while scoring residual Hericium phenotype.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Experimental Design
content_blocks.content: Preferred design: Same-panel PC12 neurite-outgrowth assay locking NGF-class positive control ± named TrkA inhibitor (e.g., K252a, GW441756) or neutralizing NGF antibody vs Hericium extract (or named hericenone/erinacine prep) ± same block, before treating NGF/TrkA as necessary for Hericium phenotype. Assay identity pre-specified as neurite-bearing % or neurite length class. α/N pre-specified. Optional rodent cognitive overlay only after cell abolish×residual locks. Optional BDNF overlay (Li) is adjacent only. Estimated kill_cost_tier=1, time_to_refute=4 weeks, ip_class=ngf-insufficiency, vault_hold=no.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Refute if: On the pre-registered PC12 neurite-outgrowth panel, under NGF neutralization or TrkA blockade that abolishes NGF-class neurite gain, residual Hericium neurite phenotype falls below 50% of Hericium-alone (neurite-bearing % or neurite length units as pre-specified) — so NGF/TrkA-sufficiency for Hericium neurite phenotype survives and ngf-insufficiency fails — when block-abolish, Hericium-alone comparator, and power/assay artifacts that would otherwise leave the test inconclusive are ruled out.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations and Caveats
content_blocks.content:
1. N1–N16 do not prove N17. N2 mapped cognition without NGF PD + cell NGF + BDNF≠NGF and left 'block NGF/TrkA → lose benefit?' as open UNKNOWN — not a matched residual-under-block H2H. N15 is residual modafinil PVT under DAT-matched block. N16 is plasma-Cr↑ without ³¹P PCr fails SD WM.
2. Potentiation / TrkA-pathway ≠ residual-under-block H2H. Zhang 26481911 potentiates NGF-mediated outgrowth; adjacent Zhang 28758954 / Phan 25288148 / Rupcic 33066380 are TrkA/Erk potentiation, partial K252a on hericenone+low-NGF, or TrkA-dependent erinacine C — none co-design NGF-class positive control abolished by the same block while scoring residual Hericium phenotype.
3. Human Mori/Li/Saitsu cognition arms lack NGF/TrkA PD and lack block arms.
4. Competing caveats: block fails to abolish NGF-class gain / Hericium-alone null / underpowered strata / assay-identity mismatch leave the test inconclusive rather than refuted.
5. NOT MB/MAOI (SERIES_FROZEN). Do not burn ip_class=none.

key_findings: Execution status is NOT_RUN — no experimental data has been generated; this is a hypothesis/assay proposal at TRL 1.
Central hypothesis: Hericium erinaceus extract retains residual PC12 neurite phenotype ≥50% of Hericium-alone under NGF neutralization or TrkA blockade that abolishes an NGF-class positive control.

Literature baseline confirms: (1) human MCI RCT cognition benefit without NGF PD (PMID 18844328); (2) cell/animal NGF induction by H. erinaceus (PMID 18758067); (3) mild-AD RCT with BDNF (not NGF) biomarkers (PMID 32581767); (4) PC12 NGF-potentiation by Hericium constituents (PMID 26481911).

Key gap identified: matched residual-Hericium under NGF/TrkA block that abolishes NGF-class neurite gain = UNKNOWN; soft-complete search found 0 true co-panel studies; anti-NGF ∩ Hericium = 0 in literature.

Proposed assay: same-panel PC12 neurite-outgrowth with NGF-class positive control ± TrkA inhibitor (K252a/GW441756) or neutralizing NGF Ab vs Hericium extract ± same block; assay identity pre-specified (neurite-bearing % or neurite length); α/N pre-specified.
Refutation threshold: residual Hericium neurite <50% of Hericium-alone under block that abolishes NGF-class gain would support NGF/TrkA-sufficiency and refute ngf-insufficiency hypothesis.
Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; kill_cost_tier=1; ip_class=ngf-insufficiency.
Adjacent potentiation studies (Zhang 28758954, Phan 25288148, Rupcic 33066380) do not satisfy the co-design requirement of abolishing NGF-class gain while scoring residual Hericium phenotype.
Status label: NEGATIVE (polarity: negative) — indicating the hypothesis is framed as an assumption-kill with no current positive evidence for the residual phenotype claim.
